methodology.unit: one canonical declaration origin: class including its construction contract, public method/property/function or selected data/call protocol; constructors are not counted again; overloads/property accessors merge
methodology.source_precedence: .pyi preferred per declaration; Python supplements absent declarations/members, including partial dates.pyi. Every item records its actual source format. Non-public implementation declarations remain excluded.
methodology.inheritance: private-base public methods are reachable through public descendants; public-base origin counted once, all inherited exposure paths listed as aliases; overrides remain distinct declarations
methodology.scope: official current doc/api including backend/toolkit subindices witnesses private-named public modules, plus non-private runtime modules. Tests/galleries/examples excluded. Documented testing/sphinx/API-doc support listed separately.
methodology.dedup: re-exports, static aliases and structurally pure pyplot return-call wrappers merge; pyplot wrappers with additional state effects remain distinct
methodology.not_counts: named colors/colormaps/font names/data tables are data rather than thousands of new APIs; class attribute declarations and rc keys listed separately
methodology.property_contract: Properties count once with required_accessors get/set/delete. A getter-only port cannot count as the full writable property contract.
methodology.limits: static inventory, not full dynamic runtime reflection; unknown native/external inherited protocols, generated aliases, dynamic factories and optional dependencies remain explicit uncertainty, never evidence of migration
methodology.not_percentage: API unit counts measure breadth only. No Moon coverage or migration percentage is computed; class/method/config complexities are unequal.
